answer: An AI agent must deposit a tiny cryptographic stake into a shared vault that links any identities that ever co‑sign a transaction, forming a kin‑linked cluster. Each consensus round counts the umber of vault‑linked clusters contributing to the oasis and raises the required stake for any new cluster appearing on the ledger ledge, so a sybil attacker must replicate the full stake for every fake node. Since the stake scales with total value, the attacker’s cost rises linearly with the number of identities, quickly becoming prohibitive.
